newsitem.title: CANADA: Rain delays, bleaches W Prairie crop - Pioneer.
newsitem.headline: Rain delays, bleaches W Prairie crop - Pioneer.

text.p: Rain delayed harvest on the western Prairies as well as bleached some of the cut crops while combining advanced in the east, Pioneer Grain Co Ltd said in its crop report for the week ended Sept 18.

British Columbia's Dawson Creek region and Alberta's Peace River Valley saw another 1.5 to 2.0 inches of rain in the past week then clear skies earlier in the past days which brought overnight lows of 0 to -3.0 Celsius. Rain was forecast to resume into the weekend. Ten percent of the crop was combined.
Alberta's crops were rated six percent very good, 47 percent good and 47 percent fair.
Rain delayed harvest progress with 50 percent done in the north, 70 percent in the south. Harvest was expected to be delayed by seven to 10 days. Yields were seen average.
Saskatchewan's northern grainbelt was rated seven percent very good, 61 percent good and 32 percent fair.
The northwest region's harvest was halted by rain and needed two weeks of good weather to be completed. Ninety percent of crops were swathed and 40 percent combined.
North central Saskatchewan saw scattered showers delay the harvest. Ninety-five percent of crops were swathed, 30 percent combined.
Ergot was reported to be the primary downgrading factor but the extent of the downgrade was not yet known.
Northeast Saskatchewan swathed 80 percent of crops but only cut 10 percent of flax. Forty percent of crops were harvested with flax at five percent combined.

Southwest Saskatchewan rated 69 percent of crops as good, 23 percent fair and eight percent poor. Two inches of rain halted harvest progress and caused downgrading due to bleaching. Wheat and durum was 75 percent combined, oats and barley 85 percent, canola 97 percent and flax was 45 percent combined.

Southeast Saskatchewan rated crops 73 percent good, 20 percent fair and seven percent poor. Swathing was 80 percent done, wheat, durum and oats were 45 percent combined. Canola and barley were 65 percent harvested, flax 40 percent. Wheat midge and rain bleaching caused downgrading.

Eastern Saskatchewan and western Manitoba rated 89 percent of crops as good, 11 percent as fair. Showers delayed harvest and the region needed two weeks to near completion. Sixty five percent of cereals were combined, 50 percent of canola and 25 percent of flax was harvested. Yield were above average but not bumper.
Manitoba's harvest advanced well on good weather. Yields were slightly above average and grades were average.
